source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten references. IoC, Observer, Reactor, and callback foundations were checked against Fowler, Design Patterns, and POSA2. Current synchronous listener ordering and error behavior were checked against Node.js 26.8.1; DOM dispatch against the current WHATWG DOM standard; cancellation/request semantics against libuv 1.x; and callable cardinality against Rust 1.98.0 Fn/FnMut/FnOnce/AsyncFnOnce documentation. FFI claims remain language/ABI-specific.

evidence: Definitions and Notation defines terminal indicators S_o/F_o/C_o/D_o, T_o, subscription q, E_q, and queue/service timing L/C.
State transitions PENDING to exclusive terminals and ACTIVE/CLOSING/CLOSED are used consistently throughout.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Cardinality, terminal, timing, and state-machine notation was reviewed; one-shot and many-event claims are not conflated.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/CONPAR-032/report.json records first A/B/C, second A/C/D, four registrations, one removal, and three active listeners.
Manual replay confirms snapshot membership remains length three while one removal and one addition change only the next emission.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Listener counts, mutation counts, and exact delivery order agree with the deterministic model.

evidence: Exactly-once terminal arbitration re-derives T_o=S_o+F_o+C_o+D_o=1 with mutually exclusive zero/one indicators.
At-most-once weakens the equality to T_o<=1 and therefore requires a separate missing-completion policy.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The algebra matches the state machine and does not imply delivery if the contract only promises at-most-once.

evidence: Reviewed inline/deferred timing, zero/one/duplicate/many delivery, throw/reject, recursive dispatch, listener mutation, and sync versus async handlers.
Reviewed unsubscribe while queued/in-flight, timeout/completion races, capture leaks, borrowed expiry, worker/UI affinity, FFI unwind/unload, overload, shutdown, and safety-critical transfer.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary review spans temporal, cardinality, membership, ownership, failure, concurrency, ABI, capacity, and deployment risks.

evidence: One-shot operations transition out of PENDING once; only the terminal winner delivers and releases capacity, while losers dispose late resources.
Subscription delivery is permitted only while active under the declared weak/strong unsubscribe policy, with captures retained through queued/in-flight retirement.
invariant_checking.notes: Invariants were checked across initiation failure, success, error, timeout, cancellation, callback failure, recursive close, and shutdown.

evidence: Snapshot dispatch proof fixes current membership before untrusted invocation, so mutation cannot invalidate iteration or alter current order.
The terminal-arbitration proof maps each competing path to one state transition and makes duplicate suppression evidence-visible.
proof_review.notes: Proofs are scoped to stated policies and do not claim all event systems, schedulers, FFI boundaries, or runtimes behave alike.

evidence: Node EventEmitter behavior is explicitly presented as one current API contract, not universal callback semantics.
Executable limitations state the model omits concurrency, errors, async handlers, FFI, cancellation, backpressure, and reclamation.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Specification facts, state-machine arguments, deterministic model evidence, API design guidance, and external review boundaries remain distinct.

evidence: python3 tools/verify_snippets.py CONPAR-032 passed the snapshot model with exact stdout and empty stderr.
Thread timing, queue delay, service duration, overload, FFI behavior, and device delivery are explicitly empirical.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The run validates one synchronous snapshot policy only and proves no real runtime scheduling or lifetime property.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed IoC, callback categories, timing/cardinality, reentrancy, listener mutation, terminal arbitration, error channels, async listeners, capture/borrow lifetime, affinity, cancellation, FFI, backpressure, composition, adaptation, and compatibility. Each concept has a clear owner.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed always-deferred versus synchronous APIs, state-before-callback rules, snapshot/tombstone dispatch, duplicate evidence, disposable tokens, generation checks, strong/weak unsubscribe, FFI drain/unload, bounded fan-out, callback-to-future/stream adapters, deterministic tests, observability, and versioning.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet gives a complete contract checklist; exposition moves from inversion through state, ownership, failure, and adapters; ten examples serve distinct purposes; exercises progress from recall to clinical/FFI transfer with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring and verification evidence only; no external runtime, ABI, language, practitioner, clinical, hardware, security, regulatory, real-time, or functional-safety review is claimed. The snapshot model does not establish concurrent dispatch, cancellation, FFI, backpressure, lifetime, timing, or deployment correctness.
